title: Adaptive residency scheduler for paged-attention and token-cache reclamation
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Background: Paged attention and large token KV caches enable long-context workloads but create fragmentation and uneven residency pressure across shards. This ticket implements an adaptive residency scheduler plus a reclamation policy that prioritizes reuse probability and decode latency impact instead of simple LRU-like heuristics. Goals: (1) reduce tail decode latency regressions caused by mid-request prefill evictions, (2) lower steady-state GPU memory usage via compacted residency windows, (3) improve reuse of recently-prefilled fragments to avoid repeated expensive prefill operations. Scope: residency residency-tracking, eviction scoring function, soft-reservations for active decodes, prefill-aware kernel coplacement hints, and an opt-in rollout with telemetry. Out of scope: cross-node live-migration and offline compaction that requires model reloading. Approach summary: - Maintain per-fragment metadata: last-prefill-time, estimated-reuse-prob (from short-window telemetry), decode-horizon (remaining tokens), residency-score. - Residency scheduler assigns soft-reservations to fragments used by in-flight decodes; reservations can be forgivable for low-priority requests. - Eviction score = w1*reuse_prob + w2*(decode_horizon_inverse) + w3*fragment_compactability - w4*prefill_cost_estimate. Weights tunable via runtime flags and autosuggest from Optimize. - Kernel hinting: when a fragment is soft-reserved, co-schedule prefill and decode kernels on the same device to avoid remote prefill costs and excessive KV-churn. - Graceful fallback: if eviction must free memory mid-prefill, prefer spilling to compressed/quantized shard variant or fall back to smaller-context model variant. Testing and validation: microbenchmarks for synthetic prefix+decode patterns, perf runs on representative customer workloads, A/B rollout with canary at 5% then 25% before full rollout. Observability: new dashboard tracking residency churn, prefill-frequency per fragment, decode re-prefill rate, p50/p95 decode latency with/without reservations. Acceptance criteria enumerated below.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency increase <= 5% on standard long-context benchmark when enabled
steady-state GPU memory footprint reduced by >= 12% on mixed prefix workloads versus baseline
re-prefill rate (same fragment prefills within 30s) reduced by >= 30%
no customer-facing errors introduced; rollback path validated via runtime flag
instrumentation: residency churn and eviction scoring visible in console dashboards
